claims.text: Chemical disorder in HfNbTaTiZr produces local lattice distortions.
Thermal activation above room temperature amplifies local lattice distortions and anharmonic lattice vibrations.
Elevated-temperature local lattice distortions cause nonlinear stress–strain behavior.
Elevated-temperature local lattice distortions increase thermal expansion relative to the room-temperature state.
Elevated-temperature local lattice distortions reduce the elastic modulus relative to the room-temperature state.
The room-temperature disordered HfNbTaTiZr alloy has a BCC or near-BCC structure.
HfNbTaTiZr retains a solid, disordered phase without a major phase transition from approximately 300 K to 1500 K.
The anharmonic contribution associated with local atomic distortions increases with temperature.
Local atomic distortions modify interatomic forces.
Modified interatomic forces produce anomalous thermal expansion.
Modified interatomic forces cause elastic softening and reduced stiffness under stress.
Elevated-temperature stress–strain curves will show reduced yield strength relative to the 300 K baseline.
Elevated-temperature stress–strain curves will show lower elastic moduli relative to the 300 K baseline.
Thermal expansion coefficients will increase with temperature because of enhanced atomic vibrations.
Changes in yield strength, elastic modulus, and thermal expansion will correlate with the onset of pronounced local lattice distortions.
At approximately 300 K, the alloy exhibits minimal anharmonic behavior and lower thermal expansion coefficients than at elevated temperature.
Above approximately 1500 K, phase transitions, creep, or grain-boundary effects may dominate the response.
